a biologically motivated artificial neuromolecular information processing system is able to differentiate and determine significant and insignificant examination data, and combinations of examination data for the diagnosis of chronic HBV infection.
the system is able to: (1) learn and differentiate data, (2) determine the significance of each examination item, and (3) determine the effectiveness of each item's combination.
the system can be effectively used to differentiate chronic hepatitis B patients from healthy individuals and hepatitis B carriers from non-carriers.

developing a biologically motivated artificial neuromolecular information system for data differentiation and parameter analysis.
developing a system for the diagnosis of chronic HBV infection based on the analysis of a clinical database.
the application of a novel biologically motivated system in the diagnosis of chronic hepatits B.
